summary.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 25% YoY to Rs.321 crore, a record quarter, but EBITDA margin was 17.6% as Moshi WtE power remained suspended.
summary.overview: Operating revenue grew 25% YoY to Rs.321 crore in Q2 FY27 and H1 revenue rose 15% to Rs.582 crore, driven by the new Mumbai operations, higher contract volumes and recognition of cost escalation. Power generation at the PCMC Moshi waste-to-energy plant has been suspended since a July incident, with restoration now expected by December 2026. Q2 EBITDA was Rs.58 crore (17.6% margin), held back by a one-time escalation-related ECL provision and the absence of Moshi power sales, which management says are temporary. Management reiterated ~20% revenue CAGR guidance over three to five years and guided Rs.290-300 crore as the base quarterly revenue ex one-offs.

segments.name: Collection & Transportation (C&T)
segments.commentary: H1 revenue Rs.394 crore, up 26% YoY and 66% of revenue (vs 60% last year). Q2 C&T volumes rose 12% to about 0.6 million tonnes.

segments.name: MSW processing
segments.commentary: Processing volumes fell 7% to 0.68 million tonnes in Q2 and H1 revenue fell 14% to Rs.124 crore; share of revenue 21% (vs 28%), mainly from no Moshi power sales.

segments.name: Other operating income
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs.65 crore, up 32% YoY; 11% of H1 revenue. Includes RDF, compost, EPR, interest and sweeping income, plus contract revenue from DBOOT capex.

segments.name: Construction & demolition (Mumbai)
segments.commentary: H1 revenue about Rs.18 crore; daily intake rose from about 250 to 450-475 tonnes, with 96% recycling rate; FY27 C&D revenue guided at Rs.34-38 crore.

segments.name: RDF
segments.commentary: Q2 sales grew 23% to about 49,000 tonnes; H1 about 89,000 tonnes.

guidance_outlook: Reiterated ~20% revenue CAGR over next three to five years.
Expects double-digit revenue growth for FY27 over FY26, supported by ongoing projects and AP construction revenue.
Moshi WtE expected to be functional by December 2026; management said December 'will definitely be done'.
Core EBITDA expected back to about 22-23% from Q1 FY28; reported EBITDA margin to recover toward historical 23-25% by FY28/FY29 on a full-year basis.
Base quarterly revenue of Rs.290-300 crore ex one-time escalation, rising once BMC contract is fully commissioned in Q4.
AP waste-to-energy projects expected to start power revenue from Q1 FY29; contract revenue of about Rs.300 crore expected in FY28 (about Rs.700 crore over 2.5 years on Rs.670-680 crore capex).
Each AP project expected to generate Rs.70-75 crore top line per year once commissioned (~20 months away); Mumbai C&T full operationalisation to add about Rs.80 crore.
Hurdle returns on PPP projects of 11-14% (ROIC/ROCE basis).
capex_capacity: Moshi WtE (PCMC): power generation suspended since July incident; MRF and composting resumed, processing about 33,600 tonnes in Q2; restoration with OEM partners, target December 2026.
Moshi restoration delay attributed to Hormuz Strait shipping embargoes; parts now being airlifted.
AP waste-to-energy projects: capex about Rs.670-680 crore; civil work started after monsoon; revenue from Q1 2029.
Mumbai BMC C&T contract capex ongoing; expected fully commissioned in Q4 FY27.
Depreciation rising from Mumbai MCGM contract; management does not foresee major jump in depreciation or interest from new Atkoli project, whose capex is reimbursed.
demand_pricing: Q2 revenue includes about Rs.40 crore of one-time escalation; part of the escalation was approved by client for past periods.
Escalation revenue triggered Rs.27 crore ECL provision under Ind AS 109, reversible as collections come in; this drove a ~27% rise in other operating expense.
Management says most cities have already outsourced C&T; waste processing has long been private-sector led via long-term concessions/BOTs.

Pipeline: bids in processing and C&T; pickup expected after November; North India bids include sanitary landfill and mechanical sweeping; south India WtE projects; western zone C&T tenders not yet issued.
New verticals: pest management and deep cleaning growing; PET bottle collection and baling for an FMCG client started in one city, three more cities soon; talks with large private townships.
CBG: in discussions with OMCs, no deal yet; also developing CBG with municipalities.
Receivables: Rs.474 crore at Sep 2026 vs Rs.402 crore at FY26 end; post-quarter collections of about Rs.108 crore; management says rolling DSO 74-80 days, historical range 90-115 days.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue and outlook for construction & demolition segment in H1 and FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 C&D revenue about Rs.18 crore; tonnage ramped from 250 to 450-475 per day, expected to stabilise near 500; FY27 C&D revenue guided at Rs.34-38 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Receivables rising and cash conversion weak; when will it improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about Rs.108 crore collected post-quarter; collections improve November to January but dry up around budget year-end; DSO historically 90-115 days; escrow and client selection (quarterly-paying clients) used to manage working capital.

qa_highlights.question: Hurdle rate for new projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Hurdle rates over project life of 11-14% ROIC/ROCE; bids are competitive PPP tenders and weigh counterparty and receivable risk.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins return to 20%+?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called Q1 and Q2 margin falls temporary: Q1 due to bio-mining project closure disposal costs, Q2 due to ECL provisioning; recovery depends on Moshi restart and Mumbai C&T traction.

qa_highlights.question: Is double-digit FY27 growth achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said current projects and AP construction revenue support double-digit growth in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is Rs.300 crore quarterly revenue sustainable and what is the base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Rs.290-300 crore should be the base after excluding about Rs.40 crore one-time escalation; Q4 expected to be the base for growth as BMC contract is fully commissioned.

qa_highlights.question: Insurance cover and further PCMC charges in Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Partially covered by insurance; survey ongoing so Rs.20 crore booked as exceptional. Management said expenses were fully booked in Q2 with no further incremental charges expected in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Finance cost decline and PAT outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 had Rs.6.8 crore refinancing cost absent in Q2; borrowing cost has eased; tax rate about 27%; EBITDA to PAT conversion expected to stay healthy.

risks_watch: Moshi WtE restart: power generation still suspended; December 2026 target depends on airlifted OEM parts after Hormuz shipping disruption.
Receivables: Rs.474 crore at Sep 2026 and DSO of 114 days (analyst cited 121); seasonal collection dips around municipal budget year-end.
Rs.27 crore ECL provision on escalation receivables; reversal depends on client collections.
Margin recovery: reported EBITDA will look softer as low-margin contract revenue (about Rs.300 crore in FY28) rises.
Insurance recovery on Rs.20 crore PCMC exceptional item remains pending survey.
Order inflow: management expects pipeline traction only after November; no new large order announced on the call.
Dividend and valuation: first maiden dividend paid; an individual investor raised concern over market cap erosion; no buyback announced.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and order visibility, but defensive on margins and receivables; management repeatedly called the margin compression temporary and accounting-driven, and declined to disclose bid return thresholds beyond a 11-14% range.

growth.why: Management guides double-digit FY27 revenue growth (midpoint ~12% used) and reiterates ~20% 3-5 year CAGR, backed by ~Rs.18,000 crore order book, Mumbai BMC contract commissioning in Q4 FY27 and Moshi restart targeted December 2026, but AP WtE capacity only arrives in FY29 and no clear quantified bridge for the CAGR was given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides core EBITDA back to ~22-23% from Q1 FY28 (Q2 reported 17.6%, H1 17.2%) once Moshi power restarts and the Rs.27 crore ECL provision reverses, though low-margin AP/C&T contract revenue (~Rs.300 crore in FY28) will dilute reported margins.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Mumbai BMC C&T contract is under construction for full commissioning in Q4 FY27 and Moshi WtE is targeted functional by December 2026; AP WtE capacity (Rs.670-680 crore capex) only arrives around Q1 FY29, outside the window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: C&T volumes rose 12% to ~0.6 Mt in Q2 and Mumbai C&D intake rose from ~250 to 450-475 tonnes/day, while processing fell 7% to 0.68 Mt on the Moshi suspension; volume growth depends on Moshi restart and BMC ramp.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is not disclosed, the AP projects (Rs.670-680 crore) are already committed, and management said bids are being pursued (North India, south India WtE), so a fresh capex announcement is conditional on winning tenders; the western zone C&T tenders are not yet issued.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management only reiterated the ~20% three-to-five-year revenue CAGR and double-digit FY27 growth, with Rs.290-300 crore base quarterly revenue ex one-offs; no raise was signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Moshi restart depends on airlifted OEM parts after Hormuz shipping disruption, and receivables of Rs.474 crore (DSO 114 days, analyst cited 121) could delay collections and reversal of the Rs.27 crore ECL provision.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: PET bottle collection and baling for an FMCG client started in one city with three more cities soon, pest management and deep cleaning are growing, and CBG talks with OMCs are ongoing with no deal yet.

rows.label: Pipeline bids pickup after November
rows.why: Order book is about Rs.18,000 crore and bids in processing, C&T and North/South India projects are pending, but management said pickup expected only after November and no new large order was announced on the call.

rows.label: Receivables and DSO normalisation
rows.why: Receivables rose to Rs.474 crore from Rs.402 crore at FY26 end, with about Rs.108 crore collected post-quarter; management says rolling DSO is 74-80 days against a 90-115 day historical range, but collections dry up around budget year-end.

rows.label: Lower finance cost post refinancing
rows.why: Q1 carried Rs.6.8 crore refinancing cost that is absent in Q2, and net debt is Rs.386 crore (0.4x net debt-to-equity) at about 10% cost of debt.
